questions.q: What does the If Condition activity require its expression to evaluate to?
options: A string matching one of several cases
questions.explain: If Condition evaluates one expression to true or false, then runs the corresponding True or False set of activities.

questions.q: What does the Switch activity's expression need to evaluate to?
options: A string value, matched against defined cases
questions.explain: Switch evaluates an expression to a string, then runs whichever case's activities match that value, or the default activities if nothing matches.

questions.q: When would you reach for Switch instead of nesting multiple If Conditions?
options: When there are three or more distinct outcomes from one value — nested If Conditions get hard to read
Switch and If Condition are functionally identical in every scenario
Only when there are exactly two possible outcomes
Switch activities can't have a default case, so use nested Ifs instead
questions.explain: Switch expresses many outcomes from one expression flatter and more legibly than nesting an If Condition inside another If Condition's false branch, repeatedly.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of cases a Switch activity supports?
questions.explain: A Switch activity supports a maximum of 25 cases. Needing more than that is usually a sign the routing logic belongs in a Lookup-driven table instead.

questions.q: What runs in a Switch activity when the expression doesn't match any defined case?
options: The pipeline fails immediately with no explanation
The first case's activities, as a fallback
Nothing — Switch requires an exact match or it throws a compile error
questions.explain: Default activities handle anything that doesn't match any of the defined cases, ensuring the Switch always has somewhere to go.
